hero.headline: Jupiter firefighters deploy to Venezuela for earthquake search and rescue mission
hero.body:
Two firefighters from Jupiter Fire Rescue have been deployed to Venezuela as part of a larger FEMA Urban Search and Rescue Task Force responding to earthquake relief efforts in the region. The deployment includes personnel from Jupiter, Delray Beach, and Palm Beach County fire departments, with a total task force of 80 members. The firefighters received their deployment orders with less than 24 hours notice and are expected to remain in Venezuela for at least two weeks.

The team's mission centers on search and rescue operations in collapsed structures, including both large buildings and smaller residential homes. To support this work, the firefighters brought specialized equipment designed for breaking through debris, cutting materials, breaching barriers, and stabilizing unsafe structures. They also brought technical rope rescue tools to assist in extracting survivors from difficult-to-reach locations within damaged buildings.

Stephen Shaw, deputy fire chief of operations for Jupiter Fire Rescue, emphasized that the deployment demonstrates the department's core commitment to assisting people in crisis situations. "This right here represents one of these situations where they need help people need help and for us at Jupiter Fire Rescue, if someone needs help we go," Shaw said. He noted that international deployments like this one are part of the department's larger mission to support communities facing emergencies.

Shaw also highlighted how the deployment will benefit Jupiter Fire Rescue internally when the team returns home. The experience gained through working on rescue operations in Venezuela will provide valuable training and skill development for the firefighters involved. "And when they come back the learning that has taken place and the skills that they have been practicing is only going to benefit us internally as we continue to grow our fire department," Shaw said. The firefighters deployed on Sunday and are currently conducting active rescue operations in Venezuela.

cards.headline: DeSantis expected to sign final state budget Monday, ending veto leverage
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis is expected to sign the state budget Monday, marking the last budget he will sign before leaving office in January. Once he signs, his most powerful tool for controlling the legislature disappears. The line-item veto power, which DeSantis has used to strike funding for projects backed by lawmakers who opposed him, will no longer influence legislative behavior after the budget is signed.

The $114.5 billion budget came after the Legislative Session extended past its 60-day calendar for the second consecutive year. House Speaker Daniel Perez and Senate President Ben Albritton disagreed fundamentally on spending levels. Perez said the House believed the state should spend less money, while the Senate believed it should spend more. The House opened at $113.6 billion and the Senate at $115 billion, with the $1.4 billion gap consuming the spring session. Both chambers' tax packages collapsed, resulting in a tax-cut deal worth roughly $300 million. The Senate passed the final budget unanimously while the House approved it 99-6. Lawmakers were then called back for a Special Session focused on the governor's property tax plan. Throughout negotiations, DeSantis maintained the threat of at least $800 million in cuts.

In May, addressing the Federalist Society, DeSantis openly acknowledged using the veto pen against members who cross him because it helps advance a legislative agenda. Every local project became leverage to enforce compliance. The property tax fight, injected into budget season, operated as another tool to pressure votes. DeSantis spent the weekend on social media highlighting his record, posting that Florida has the fewest state workers per capita in the country, fewer than when he took office in 2019, and noting this marks the fourth straight year of reducing the budget.

Despite losing budget veto power Monday, DeSantis will continue wielding significant executive authority until his last day in office. He will continue filling judicial positions and making hundreds of appointments to state and local boards, water management districts, university trusteeships, and licensing panels. He intends to stack these positions with loyalists who will carry his agenda forward. DeSantis will also lead the campaign for Amendment 3, the homestead exemption measure his legislature sent to voters, which requires 60 percent approval in November. While the budget veto power ends Monday, his influence through appointments and judicial selections continues through his final day in office.

cards.headline: Woman, 78, killed after SUV rolls backward in Port St. Lucie driveway
cards.teaser: A 78-year-old woman was killed Sunday morning after an SUV rolled backward and struck her in a residential driveway in Port St.
cards.body:
A 78-year-old woman was killed Sunday morning after an SUV rolled backward and struck her in a residential driveway in Port St. Lucie, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The incident happened at approximately 10:47 a.m. when a 2016 Lincoln MKX SUV was parked in a residential driveway and the woman was standing outside the vehicle near the open driver's door. The SUV began rolling backward, and the open door struck her, knocking her to the ground. Her adult son, 59, was in the passenger seat and had started the vehicle. The cause of the rollback remains under investigation.

The woman was rushed to Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce, where she was pronounced deceased at 11:19 a.m. Neighbor Daisy Cardona, who had known the woman for several years, witnessed the emergency response. "I saw the ambulance, the fire trucks, and two or three police cars," Cardona said. "On Sundays, they would bring us bread, cupcakes, donuts, and sometimes cakes that were this big. May she rest in peace and my condolences to her family." The incident remains under investigation.

cards.headline: AFSCME Florida wins recertification votes across state despite union restrictions
cards.teaser: Three years after Florida enacted sweeping restrictions on public-sector unions, AFSCME Florida continues posting lopsided recertification victories, with workers in Jacksonville, Polk County, Miami Gardens, DeFuniak Springs and Naples all voting overwhelmingly in recent weeks to retain union representation.
cards.body:
Jacksonville city employees represented by AFSCME Local 1279 voted more than 98% in favor of recertification this week, continuing a streak of overwhelming union victories across Florida. AFSCME Florida reported winning 30 of 32 recertification elections in 2025, with some wins including bargaining units that lost certification during early implementation of the 2023 law but rebuilt membership and won recognition back. This month, local AFSCME chapters scored recertification triumphs in DeFuniak Springs, Hialeah, Miami Gardens, Naples and Polk County, following earlier wins in Hallandale Beach, Miami-Dade County, Miami-Dade's Jackson Health System and Orange County.

The 2023 law, SB 256, sponsored by then-Sen. Blaise Ingoglia, hiked membership requirements for most public-sector unions from 50% of a bargaining unit to 60% and blocked automatic dues deductions. By May 2025, more than 100 unions in Florida had been decertified, with roughly 69,000 workers losing representation. Arthur Finley, President of AFSCME Local 1279, described SB 256 as massively disruptive legislation that initially led to the organization's decertification in February 2024. After re-registering hundreds of members, implementing a new dues payment system and holding dozens of meetings, Local 1279 ratified a new contract with Jacksonville by a 99% vote in September. Legislation going into effect July 1, SB 1296, requires at least 50% of a bargaining unit to vote in certification elections and mandates recertification if fewer than 60% of employees are dues-paying members.

cards.headline: Off-duty firefighter among two civilians who found diver's body off Fort Pierce coast
cards.teaser: An off-duty firefighter was among two civilians who discovered a diver's body off the Fort Pierce coast over the weekend.
cards.body:
Officials are investigating a deadly diving incident off the coast of Fort Pierce. An off-duty firefighter was among two civilians who assisted in the recovery of a diver found dead off the St. Lucie County coast Sunday.

The diver's body was found off the Fort Pierce coast. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and local authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the death.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Game Postponed Saturday, Rescheduled for Late July in Port St. Lucie
cards.body:
A scheduled matchup between the St. Lucie Mets and Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Saturday was postponed and will be rescheduled for late July at the Mets' home stadium in Port St. Lucie. The postponement announcement came Saturday evening, though officials did not immediately provide the specific date for the makeup game.

The two teams had been in the middle of a weekend series when the postponement occurred. On Friday, the Mighty Mussels dominated the Mets with a 6-2 victory, powered by four home runs. The following day, the Mussels won again by a narrow margin, edging out the Mets 6-5 in a game that featured a late rally attempt by St. Lucie.

The St. Lucie Mets operate as the Single-A affiliate of the New York Mets within the Florida State League structure. The team plays its home games at their Port St. Lucie facility, which will host the rescheduled contest whenever it takes place in late July.

Fans who purchased tickets for Saturday's postponed game should contact the St. Lucie Mets organization directly to learn about options for using those tickets at the rescheduled event. The team will provide additional information about the specific makeup date as it becomes available.

hero.teaser: The new location will join two existing Chipotle restaurants already operating in the city.
hero.body:
The new location will join two existing Chipotle restaurants already operating in the city. Port St. Lucie has seen continued commercial expansion as the population grows across St. Lucie County.

Chipotle is a fast-casual Mexican restaurant chain that offers burritos, bowls, tacos, and salads. The company operates multiple locations throughout Florida.

The announcement comes as Port St. Lucie continues to attract new restaurant and retail development. The specific location and opening date for the third Chipotle have not been disclosed.

cards.headline: MusicWorks in Vero Beach launches fourteenth concert season
cards.teaser: Vero Beach's MusicWorks has launched its fourteenth concert season with programming designed to expand cultural tourism and attract visitors from multiple states.
cards.body:
MusicWorks in Vero Beach has begun its fourteenth concert season with performances aimed at expanding cultural tourism in Indian River County. The organization's programming is designed to inspire multi-state travel from California, Texas, New York, Tennessee, Georgia, Illinois, Nevada, Arizona, Michigan, and Massachusetts.

The concert series is part of efforts to attract visitors to Vero Beach through cultural offerings. MusicWorks has operated as a cultural institution in the community for over a decade.

The season launch positions Vero Beach alongside other states in cultural programming efforts. The specific concert schedule and venues were not detailed in the announcement.

cards.headline: Three seats on Indiantown Village Council up for election August 18
cards.teaser: Three of five seats on the Indiantown Village Council will be decided in an August 18 election in Martin County.
cards.body:
Three seats on the Indiantown Village Council are up for election on August 18. The races represent three of the five total seats on the governing body for the Martin County community.

Indiantown voters will decide who represents them on the village council for the upcoming term. The election will determine the makeup of the council that oversees local government operations.

The August 18 election date is set for Indiantown residents to cast ballots.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County commissioner defends seat in general election
cards.teaser: A St. Lucie County commissioner is running to defend their seat in the upcoming general election.
cards.body:
A St. Lucie County commissioner is seeking reelection in the general election. The incumbent faces a challenge for their seat on the county commission that governs St. Lucie County.

The county commission oversees land use, budget, and policy decisions affecting Port St. Lucie, Fort Pierce, and unincorporated areas of St. Lucie County. Commission seats are countywide positions.

The general election will determine who represents the district on the St. Lucie County Commission. The specific commissioner, district number, and challenger information were not provided in the election notice.

cards.headline: Florida candidates for state House answer 2026 election questions
cards.teaser: Candidates running for Florida state House seats have responded to questions about their positions ahead of the 2026 election.
cards.body:
Candidates for Florida state House seats have answered questions about their platforms and positions for the 2026 election cycle. The responses provide voters with information about candidates seeking to represent districts in the state legislature.

State House representatives make decisions on education, transportation, environmental policy, and budget matters that affect Treasure Coast residents. Florida House District 84 covers portions of Martin and St. Lucie counties, while District 54 includes parts of Indian River County.

The 2026 election will determine which candidates serve in the Florida House of Representatives. Specific candidates, districts, and question topics were not detailed in the announcement.

cards.teaser: A Florida mayor will face two challengers in a contested election scheduled for November 3.
cards.body:
A Florida mayor is running for reelection against two challengers in a November 3 election. The contested race will determine who leads the municipality for the next term.

The three-way race gives voters a choice between the incumbent mayor and two candidates seeking to unseat the current officeholder. Municipal elections determine local leadership on issues including public safety, infrastructure, and community development.

The November 3 election date is set for voters to decide the mayoral race. The specific city, mayor's name, and challenger identities were not provided in the election notice.

hero.headline: Fort Myers Mighty Mussels Beat St. Lucie Mets 6-5 in Sunday Contest
hero.teaser: The Fort Myers Mighty Mussels held off a late rally by the St. Lucie Mets to win 6-5 on Sunday in Port St. Lucie.
hero.body:
The Mighty Mussels survived a late comeback attempt by the St. Lucie Mets to secure a 6-5 victory on Sunday. The game was played in Port St. Lucie.

The Mets mounted a rally late in the game but fell short of completing the comeback. The Mussels held on for the win to take the series.

This was the third game of the weekend series between the two Florida State League teams. Fort Myers had won Friday's game 6-2 behind four home runs, while Saturday's scheduled contest was postponed and rescheduled for late July.

cards.headline: Fort Myers Slugs Four Home Runs in 6-2 Win Over St. Lucie Mets
cards.teaser: The Fort Myers Mighty Mussels hit four home runs Friday night to defeat the St. Lucie Mets 6-2 in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
The Mighty Mussels powered their way to a 6-2 victory over the St. Lucie Mets on Friday with a four-homer performance. The game was played at the Mets home stadium in Port St. Lucie.

The Mussels offense came alive with the long ball, hitting four home runs to support their pitching staff. The Mets managed just two runs in the loss.

The win was the first of a three-game weekend series between the two Florida State League clubs. Saturday's game was later postponed and rescheduled for late July.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Florida Highwaymen Museum Featured in America 250 Road Trip
cards.teaser: The Florida Highwaymen Museum in Fort Pierce has been selected as a featured stop on the America 250 Road Trip celebrating the nation's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
The Florida Highwaymen Museum, which opened this year in Fort Pierce, has been announced as a featured stop on the America 250 Road Trip celebrating the country's 250th birthday. Located at 1234 Avenue D, the museum is the nation's only one with exhibitions that include paintings from each of the 26 renowned Highwaymen artists.

The museum celebrates 26 Black artists who began painting in the 1950s, creating bold, colorful landscapes of Florida's untouched beauty. These artists sold their work along the roadside when segregation kept them out of traditional galleries. The museum is currently open Saturday and Sunday from noon to 4 p.m. through July 31. The museum will be closed in August and reopen in September with a new exhibit. Fall and spring hours from September 1 through June 15 will be expanded.

Vero Beach's MusicWorks is launching its fourteenth concert season, aligning Florida with California, Texas, New York, Tennessee, Georgia, Illinois, Nevada, Arizona, Michigan and Massachusetts in an effort to expand cultural tourism and inspire multi-state travel. The concert series is expected to draw visitors from across the country to the Treasure Coast community.

The season launch positions Vero Beach as a cultural destination alongside major metropolitan areas. MusicWorks has established itself as a regional attraction that brings classical and contemporary performances to the area.

The concert series represents a growing segment of cultural tourism in Indian River County. Vero Beach has developed a reputation for arts programming that attracts visitors beyond its traditional seasonal population.

The fourteenth season continues MusicWorks' track record of presenting professional performances in Vero Beach. The organization has become a fixture in the local arts community over more than a decade of operations.

cards.headline: Boca Raton SoFlo Market adds patriotic celebration for July 4 at City Hall
cards.teaser: The free monthly SoFlo Market will turn Boca Raton City Hall into a Fourth of July celebration Saturday, July 4, featuring a kids parade, DJ, vendors, and free gifts for the first 20 children.
cards.body:
The popular SoFlo Market is transforming Boca Raton City Hall into a red, white and blue celebration for Independence Day on Saturday, July 4. Founder Tatiana Freitas told WPTV the free monthly event will draw families, food lovers and local shopping enthusiasts from across Palm Beach County. Highlights include a kids' parade, a DJ, unique vendors, gourmet food and free gifts for the first 20 children through the gate. Visitors can also enjoy face painting, a foggy bubble station, mini golf, balloon twisting, handmade crafts and desserts, plus a live appearance by the SoFlo Market's flamingo mascot.

Boca Raton firefighters and police officers have been invited to participate in the event. Kyle, Freitas' son, and Eddie, her husband, are part of the organizing team. The market will run from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. at Boca Raton City Hall, located at 201 West Palmetto Park Road. Electricity will be powered by generators on-site. Freitas said the market's mission is to uplift small local businesses and bring the community together. The event's Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube channels will feature behind-the-scenes clips and photos throughout the day.

cards.headline: Boca Raton George Snow Scholarship Fund awards record $7.5 million to 470 students
cards.teaser: The George Snow Scholarship Fund has awarded more than $7.5 million in scholarships and support services to 470 students across Palm Beach and Broward counties in 2026, marking a record year for the Boca Raton nonprofit.
cards.body:
The George Snow Scholarship Fund, headquartered in Boca Raton, awarded more than $7.5 million in scholarships and support services to 470 students across Palm Beach and Broward counties in 2026, according to President Tim Snow. Founded over 40 years ago, the nonprofit has distributed more than $45 million to over 4,100 students, making it the largest scholarship provider in Palm Beach County. The program bridges the gap between traditional financial aid and what students and families can afford by offering four-year commitments to ensure stability throughout college.

The fund's services extend beyond financial assistance. Vice President of Development Jay Brandt noted that GSSF provides mentorship, professional development, and resources like the College Compass podcast. Scholar Services Coordinator Garvey Antoine leads the Doyle-Whelchel Scholars Boutique, which offers professional, formal, and casual wear to help scholars prepare for interviews, internships, and campus life. Donations to the boutique include new or gently used clothing, footwear, and accessories. One 2026 recipient, Zya Chow, a Wellington Community High School graduate, earned both the Royal Palm Hearing Aid Scholarship and the Davidowitz Family Caregiving Youth Scholarship and plans to attend Georgetown University.

cards.headline: Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League issues hurricane safety tips for pet owners
cards.teaser: Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League is urging South Florida residents to create a disaster plan for their pets before the next storm hits, with hurricane season now in full swing.
cards.body:
With hurricane season in full swing, Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League is urging South Florida residents to create a disaster plan for their pets before the next storm hits. Dr. Alyssa Comroe, CEO of Peggy Adams, told WPTV the safest place for pets during a hurricane is right alongside their owners. Florida's hurricane season runs June through November, overlapping with extreme summer heat.

The shelter's expert team recommends several key steps for pet safety. Pets should wear a collar with current identification and have an updated microchip registered with correct contact information. Owners should introduce pets to a designated safe room ahead of time, such as a walk-in closet or downstairs bathroom, and conduct practice runs so the hurricane is not their first time there. Pet owners should prepare an emergency kit with a three-day supply of food and water in airtight containers, bowls, a sturdy carrier, bedding, towels, medications for two weeks, vaccination records, first-aid supplies, litter and box for cats, leashes, harnesses, cool packs, wipes, waste bags, and multiple forms of visible ID. Residents should keep a printed list of local pet-friendly shelters and hotels in an accessible place, maintain recent photos of pets ideally with their owner, and conduct hurricane drills that include pets' daily routines inside the safe room.

cards.headline: DeSantis vetoes inmate trucking program and naturopathic medicine board
cards.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis vetoed two bills Friday night, blocking a program to train nonviolent inmates as truck drivers and rejecting creation of a state naturopathic medicine board.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis vetoed HB 325 on Friday night, rejecting a bill that would have extended commercial driver's license training to nonviolent inmates with two years or less remaining on their sentences. The measure passed unanimously in both chambers but drew DeSantis's concern that training inmates to drive creates significant public safety concerns and would be unnecessarily burdensome to the Department of Corrections. Legislators countered that the program would add no new costs or strain to the prison system. According to the House bill analysis, the measure addressed the national shortage of commercial truck drivers, estimated at about 80,000 and projected to worsen as the industry replaces some 1.2 million retiring drivers over the coming decade.

DeSantis also vetoed SB 688, legislation that would have created a Board of Naturopathic Medicine within the Department of Health to set guidelines for practitioners. DeSantis has previously vetoed a bill to track e-bike and scooter crashes and a measure making it easier for high school students to volunteer as poll workers. More vetoes are expected for line items in the budget, which DeSantis is expected to sign Monday ahead of the July 1 fiscal year.

cards.headline: Orlando magician Drew Thomas brings illusions to Grande Lakes residency
cards.teaser: Drew Thomas, who appeared as a finalist on America's Got Talent Season 4, performs The Magic Show in a residency at Grande Lakes Orlando, home to Ritz-Carlton and JW Marriott hotels.
cards.body:
Drew Thomas, 57, has lived in Orlando for about a decade and performs "The Magic Show" in a residency at Grande Lakes Orlando, home to Ritz-Carlton and JW Marriott hotels. His shows are scheduled throughout the summer, with Halloween and Christmas-themed shows coming later this year. Thomas was tapped during the creative process for Epic Universe, Universal's new theme park that includes a Harry Potter expansion. He consulted on everything from character placement in the park to magical show effects, window displays and how the wands work.

Thomas has an extensive history working with Universal. He co-created Jack's Carnival of Wonders, which debuted at Halloween Horror Nights in 2007 and was revived in 2015. He grew up in Columbus, Ohio, where his grandparents fostered his love of magic by purchasing used magic books at library book sales. His first paid gig was at a child's birthday party performing balloon tricks and other magic while wearing a full leg cast, earning $150. At age 40, Thomas performed for "America's Got Talent" judges Simon Cowell, David Hasselhoff, Piers Morgan and Sharon Osbourne. His unconventional career also included playing a lead character in the Columbus Ballet's Nutcracker and developing entertainment for theme parks and cruises.

hero.headline: Salty Pelican Fish Shack in Hobe Sound Reviewed
hero.body:
A new restaurant review examines the Salty Pelican Fish Shack in Hobe Sound. The establishment serves seafood in Martin County.

The review was published Monday morning. The Salty Pelican Fish Shack operates in Hobe Sound, a coastal community in southern Martin County.
